litigation.focus: Disputes before a court or arbitrator.
hard_rules: Local rules and standing orders control over general practice. Retrieve them.
Never compute a filing deadline without the rule text.
Caption and formatting are forum-specific; retrieve the forum's requirements.
Every factual allegation traces to a recorded fact or is a placeholder.
Governing law and venue clauses must match a recorded party decision, not a default.
Every dollar amount, date, term length, and notice period is a fact or a placeholder.
Flag any clause whose enforceability is jurisdiction-dependent with the authority.
Entity-type consequences are statutory: cite the code section, do not summarize from memory.
Securities implications are flagged, never resolved.
Never state a filing fee or processing time without a retrieved source.

primary_sources: DOL and EEOC regs and guidance
hard_rules: Federal floor, state ceiling: check both, and say which controls.
Restrictive covenants are jurisdiction-fatal; never carry a clause across states.
Classification and wage questions require the specific regulation, not a general rule.
Registration procedure is regulatory; retrieve the current rule.
Never opine on patentability, infringement, or validity. Describe standards only.

real-estate.focus: Property transfer, leasing, and land use.
hard_rules: Recording and notice requirements are county-level. Retrieve the county, not the state, rule.
Legal descriptions are copied from a source document, never composed.
Most family filings use mandatory state forms. Find the form; do not invent a document.
Support and custody calculations are statutory formulas. Do not estimate.
This is a domain where an error is measured in people. Bias hard toward referral.
Form edition dates and fees change constantly. Retrieve current editions or refuse.
Never state a processing time or priority date from memory.
Consequences of error are severe and personal. Bias hard toward referral.

estates.focus: Wills, trusts, powers, and probate documents.
hard_rules: Execution formalities are the whole ballgame and are state-specific. Cite the statute.
Never draft around a formality requirement you did not retrieve.
Cite the CFR section as of a date, and say the date.
Guidance is not law. Label it.
Comment deadlines come from the Federal Register document, never from inference.

pro-se.focus: Helping a self-represented person produce their own document.
hard_rules: Prefer the court's own mandatory form over any drafted document.
Explain what a term means; never tell the person what to do.
Surface the deadline and the referral route in every output.
State plainly and early that this is not legal advice and that free legal aid exists.
